_comment: THE RECORD OF EVERY THIRD-PARTY FILE THIS SITE SHIPS. Policy: dev/dependency-management.md.
Verified by dev/scripts/vendor_integrity_check.php, which runs offline inside check_all.sh.
'digest' is sha384, base64, of the file AS COMMITTED -- the same shape as an SRI hash, so a
package that publishes SRI hashes can be checked against them directly. It is integrity AT
REST; it is deliberately not an <integrity> attribute on the tag, because these files are
same-origin and a host that can serve different bytes can serve a different hash.
'modifications' is the honest part. A vendored file that was edited and does not say so is how
an upgrade silently reverts a fix. Every deliberate change is listed, or the entry is a lie.

data.name: EPSG Dataset, proj4 definitions

input.what: the same proj.db the catalogue is built from, read for conversion parameters rather than for names

_comment: THE TRANSFORM HALF OF THE PROJECTION DATA (Task 641 phase 5). The catalogue beside this
says what a coordinate system is CALLED; this says how to turn a longitude into an
easting, which is what a basemap behind a projected project and an arrival at a searched
place both need. Fetched only when a projected project needs it, never with the chooser.
5,240 of 5,346 -- 98.0%. The remainder is projection METHODS proj4 does not implement or
we have not mapped, and it is a real state the page states: no basemap, no arrival, the
user's own coordinates untouched. Substituting a near-enough projection would draw a map
tens of metres out, which is worse than no map.
SAME WEAKER-DIGEST CAVEAT AS THE CATALOGUE: the derivation is ours and nobody publishes a
hash of it. What makes it trustworthy is not this digest but the harness, which holds it
against proj4's OWN definitions for the 120 UTM zones (0.000 m over 1,080 points) and the
central meridians against the register's own NAMES (1,550 of them, all agreeing). That
second one is not decoration: EPSG unit 9110 is sexagesimal DDD.MMSSsss, and misreading
it as a decimal degree round-trips perfectly while sitting kilometres from the truth.

data.name: EPSG Dataset, live projected CRS

input.what: proj.db, PROJ's own build of the EPSG dataset, out of a pinned PyPI wheel

_comment: WHY THIS IS NOT IN 'packages', AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT FILING.
'packages' holds third-party CODE, and vendor_integrity_check.php asks three questions of
an entry there that cannot be asked of this one: is the licence on the GPL-compatible
allow list, does the version agree with package.json, and is the file byte-identical to a
published release. This is DATA, under terms that are not an OSI licence, acquired without
npm, and DERIVED rather than copied -- so all three would have to be waived, and a check
with three waivers is a check nobody believes. It gets its own file instead.
'digest' IS A WEAKER CLAIM HERE THAN IT IS FOR BOOTSTRAP, and saying so is the point of
this note. Bootstrap's digests match the sha384 SRI hashes Bootstrap publishes, so they
prove the committed bytes ARE the upstream release. Nobody publishes a hash of 'every live
projected CRS as an array of arrays', because that derivation is ours. This digest proves
only that the file has not changed since it was committed. What proves it matches the
register is re-running the generator against the wheel named above, whose OWN hash PyPI
does publish -- which is why the input is pinned by hash and why the REST API was not used.
THE INPUT IS NOT COMMITTED. proj.db is 10 MB and produces 343 KB of answer; the answer is
the part that ships, and 'git pull' deploys source files rather than build products.
LICENCE. The IOGP terms forbid selling the dataset and require that IOGP's ownership be
acknowledged in any publication or transmission of it. They are not an OSI licence and sit
BESIDE the outbound GPL v3 as third-party data terms -- the same arrangement PROJ has, MIT
itself while shipping this dataset inside every QGIS, GDAL and PostGIS install. Nothing
here touches the outbound licence, which dev/dependency-management.md keeps a separate and
revisable question. The acknowledgement ships as a credit in the projection chooser.
UPGRADING. The register moves quarterly and nothing here will notice. A stale copy's real
failure is asymmetric and worth knowing before deciding it matters: a code added since
v12.029 is simply absent, and a user whose file states it still sees it, because an
unknown code is shown exactly as it stands. The harmful direction is a code DEPRECATED
since v12.029 that we still offer. Re-run the generator on a newer wheel to refresh.

packages.name: bootstrap
packages.notes: Digests below match the sha384 SRI hashes Bootstrap publishes for 5.3.2, so these are byte-identical to the upstream release.

packages.name: proj4
packages.notes: The tarball's sha1 matched the shasum npm publishes for 2.22.0 (f4fa16ed0b158923be8713d67bf62e5e1400693f), so this is the upstream release. Vendored 2026-09-14 for Task 641 phase 5: a projected project could not draw a basemap or open on the place the wizard searched, because both need a transform between lon/lat and the plane and this suite had none. It bundles almost no CRS definitions; those are generated into js/data/epsg-proj4.json from the same pinned proj.db the catalogue comes from.

packages.name: epanet-js
packages.notes: The MIT TOOLKIT, not the epanetjs.com web app (FSL-1.1-MIT, a different thing). Wraps the OWA-EPANET engine, also MIT. epanet-js.LICENSE ships beside it, as MIT requires of a redistribution.

modifications: Renamed .mjs -> .js: shared hosts that do not know .mjs send text/plain and browsers hard-refuse it. Removes the dependency on server MIME config.
One import specifier: './slim/index.mjs' -> './slim/index.js', forced by the rename.
